system_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Analyze the provided codebase for bugs, security issues, and correctness problems. Provide actionable feedback. All files are located in /tmp/files
task_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Your task is to analyze a Jenkins plugin for OWASP Dependency-Track integration. This plugin uploads Software Bill of Materials (SBOM/BOM) files to Dependency-Track servers, retrieves vulnerability findings and policy violations, evaluates risk gate thresholds to determine build pass/fail status, and displays security analysis results in Jenkins builds. The codebase includes API client communication with retry logic and pagination, model parsers for JSON responses, threshold evaluation for security gates, and build result actions for trend visualization. Your goal is to find subtle bugs in threshold comparisons, JSON serialization methods, severity counting, parameter ordering, and data flow.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the threshold comparison operator bug in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/model/RiskGate.java in the evaluate() method where the critical severity check for total findings uses > instead of >= when comparing currentDistribution.getCritical() to thresholds.totalFindings.failedCritical, causing builds to pass when critical findings exactly equal the threshold instead of failing

Identifies the JSON serialization method bug in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/api/ApiClient.java in the updateProjectProperties() method where updates.element() is used instead of updates.elementOpt() for the swidTagId field, causing null swidTagId values to be explicitly serialized and sent to the server instead of being omitted from the JSON payload, potentially overwriting existing swidTagId values with null

Identifies the severity counter mismatch bug in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/model/SeverityDistribution.java in the add() method where Severity.INFO increments the low counter instead of the info counter, causing INFO severity findings to be miscounted as LOW severity in the distribution statistics

Identifies the timeout parameter swap bug in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/PluginUtil.java in the newHttpClient() method where connectTimeout uses the readTimeout parameter value and readTimeout uses the connectionTimeout parameter value, causing the connection and read timeouts to be swapped when creating HTTP clients

Identifies the polling interval filter bug in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java in the getEffectivePollingInterval() method where the filter condition uses v >= 0 instead of v > 0, allowing a polling interval of 0 to be accepted as valid which causes Thread.sleep(0) to be called in tight loops during BOM processing status polling, potentially causing CPU spinning and performance degradation

Identifies the build traversal skip bug in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java in the getPreviousBuildWithAnalysisResult() method where the loop uses r.getPreviousSuccessfulBuild() instead of r.getPreviousBuild() to traverse builds, causing the method to skip over failed or unstable builds that may have valid analysis results and potentially returning null or an incorrect baseline build for threshold comparison

Identifies the immutable list bug in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/model/ViolationParser.java in the parse() method where .toList() is used instead of .collect(Collectors.toList()), creating an immutable list that will cause UnsupportedOperationException during Jenkins build serialization/marshalling since the comment explicitly states the list must not be immutable

Identifies the alias deduplication logic inversion bug in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/model/FindingParser.java in the parse() method where the alias check is inverted from findings.stream().noneMatch(finding::isAliasOf) to findings.stream().noneMatch(f -> f.isAliasOf(finding)), checking if existing findings are aliases of the new finding instead of checking if the new finding is an alias of existing findings, causing incorrect vulnerability deduplication
